messages:
Priya: Quick flag: new microquant A/B in staging shows an unusual class of structured-output corruption for funcalls — JSON parses but string args contain literal control chars or truncated escape sequences. Observed rate ~2.2% on funcall-heavy traffic (4k requests).

Priya: Example raw output from stream capture:
```
{"tool":"email.send","args":{"to":"user@example.com","subject":"Welcome","body":"Hello\u000AJohn\u2014thanks for signing up"}}
```
But some traces get delivered as:
```
{"tool":"email.send","args":{"to":"user@example.com","subject":"Welcome","body":"Hello
John—thanks for signing up"}}
```
Which is valid JSON either way, but the tool sees an actual newline in the body in the second case. That breaks downstream templates and causes side-effectful sends with malformed content.

Sam: Is this streaming-frame cut hitting inside \u escapes? Looks like tokenization shifts with quant cause partial-escape at frame boundary.

Ava: Baseline fp16 parity run showed ~0.01% of these; this is a clear regression correlated to microquant.

Marta: Major risk: silent corruption of inputs for side-effect tools. If the parser succeeds we don't trigger retry or quarantine and downstream services get garbage.

Jin: Proposal: add a light validator in postprocess that scans tool arg strings for control characters other than \n and \t and rejects or quarantines such responses when found. For quarantined responses, do NOT invoke the tool and return structured error: {"code":"TOOL_ARG_QUARANTINED"}. Log original raw output for offline analysis.

Priya: Agreed. Also add idempotency tokens for tool calls so accidental retries are safe. We need a manifest field per tool: side_effect: true/false. If side_effect=true and validator fires, always quarantine. If side_effect=false we can consider auto-repair (conservative).

Sam: For auto-repair rules: only allow re-escaping of control chars and balancing braces/quotes. Do NOT normalize escaped->literal changes. Tag all repairs with repair_type and diff in telemetry. Repair only in non-side-effectful path and only for canary-tagged runs.

Marta: I'll update telemetry: model_variant, parsed_success, quarantined, repaired, repair_type, tool_name, tool_side_effect, invoked_flag, idempotency_key, token_cut_index. Also add alert: quarantined_rate > 0.5% in 5m -> hold canary.

Priya: Operational plan: 1) deploy validator/quarantine in postprocess for canary variant (quarantine mode) 2) run 50/50 A/B (old fp16 vs microq) for 12h, 3) collect token-cut logs and repair telemetry, 4) run offline eval of 30k historical funcall prompts through microq to build taxonomy.

Jin: I'll prepare the offline run tonight and classify repairable vs unrepairable cases. Output CSV will include raw_stream_hex, token_cut_positions, and suggested repair.

Sam: Implementation notes: keep validator out of hot runtime path. Return quarantine error synchronously to client if detected. Persist original raw output and repaired result (if any) to blob store for audits. Do not surface original raw to clients.

Priya: If double-invoke detection (same idempotency_key seen twice with invoked_flag=true) > 0.3% we immediately revert.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: `microq-arg-validator-quarantine-v1` -> staging. CI: 3/5 checks passing.

Ava: Add runbook steps: how to inspect token-cut logs, how to run repair analyzer, and how to escalate to model oncall.

Marta: Oncall doc updated and alert wired. I'll also add a short note about banned auto-fixes for side-effectful tools.

Priya: Thanks team. I'll post the offline eval link and a short summary once the run finishes.

Ava: :thumbsup:
